newsitem.title: USA: N.Y.'s McCall says subpeonas sent to NYC agencies.
newsitem.headline: N.Y.'s McCall says subpeonas sent to NYC agencies.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall, who is feuding with New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani over agency audits the mayor calls politically motivated, on Tuesday said subpeonas were issued to let his work continue.
McCall will discuss the matter at a 1300 EDT news conference at his office at 270 Broadway here, according to a press release from the comproller's office.
A deal reached late last week between the comptroller, a Democrat and potential candidate for governor, and the Guiliani Administration broke done Monday.
A spokesman for Mayor Giuliani had no immediate comment.

A spokeswoman for the Republican mayor has said the state watchdog had agreed to withdraw audits that covered the police and sanitation departments, human resources and how the city was prepared to deal with computer problems that could arise at the start of 2000.
Giuliani has trumpeted his administration's success in cutting crime and putting people on welfare to work--important issues in November's mayoral election.
Randy Mastro, the deputy mayor for operations, has said some of McCall's audits raised questions about his objectivity, as they did not seem to be directed at financial issues.
But McCall's spokeswoman said the comptroller's agreement with the Giuliani Administration had cleared the way for the audits to continue.
